questions.q: Which Snowflake schema does Power BI connect to in this platform?
options: raw, so it always sees the freshest source data
prod, specifically — never raw, never dev
dev, so analysts can preview work in progress
A separate schema created just for Power BI, distinct from prod
questions.explain: PROD contains only customers and orders, the two marts that have already passed Chapter 4's tests and the Chapter 6 CI gate.

questions.q: Why would connecting Power BI to DEV instead of PROD be a real governance problem?
options: DEV schemas are always slower to query than PROD
A business user could see a developer's half-finished, untested model mid-edit, instead of only verified marts
Power BI technically cannot connect to any schema except prod
DEV schemas do not support the Snowflake Power BI connector
questions.explain: DEV is explicitly where in-progress, unverified work lives — exposing it to business users defeats the whole point of restricting BI access to PROD.

questions.q: Which role and warehouse does Power BI's connection use, and why those specifically?
options: analyst and reporting_wh — a read-only role on its own warehouse, so a refresh never competes with a dbt build for compute and can't write anywhere
sysadmin and a shared warehouse used by every tool on the platform
A brand-new role created specifically for this lesson
transformer and transforming_wh, the same ones dbt itself uses
questions.explain: analyst is read-only on prod only, and reporting_wh keeps BI query compute isolated from dbt's build workload — both decided back in Chapter 2.

questions.q: If Power BI's analyst credentials were ever compromised, what is the real blast radius under this setup?
options: Full write access to the entire Snowflake account
Access to GitHub Actions secrets and the CI pipeline
Read access to two already-verified marts (customers and orders) only — no write access anywhere, no visibility into raw or dev
The ability to delete the entire jaffle_shop_db database
questions.explain: Because analyst is scoped to read-only on prod, a compromised credential's damage is contained to viewing two trusted marts, nothing more.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say its five connection settings were "actually decided back in Chapter 2," not in this lesson?
options: Because this lesson creates all five settings from scratch for the first time
Because Power BI automatically generates these settings without any prior configuration
Because Chapter 2 and this lesson describe two completely unrelated sets of settings
Because the roles, warehouses, and schemas being used here were already built in Chapter 2 — this lesson is where they get used by an actual BI tool for the first time
questions.explain: This lesson introduces no new Snowflake objects — it's the first real consumer of the RBAC and schema decisions Chapter 2 already made.
